q: 1. The distance between steps for measuring downhill to obtain better accuracy
options: decreases with decrease of weight of the chain
explain: On steeper downhill slopes, shorter measuring steps must be taken to maintain accuracy in stepping/chaining, so the step distance decreases as slope increases.

q: 2. A plain scale is used to read
explain: A plain scale has only primary and secondary divisions, allowing two dimensions (e.g., units and tenths, such as metres and decimetres) to be read directly.

q: 3. Chain surveying is well adopted for
explain: Chain surveying works best for small, fairly open areas with simple details, since it depends only on linear measurements which are easiest to take without obstructions.

q: 4. The correction for sag is
explain: Sag in a tape suspended between supports always causes the measured length to be longer than the true straight-line distance, so the sag correction is always subtractive.

q: 5. Cross-staff is used for
explain: A cross-staff is a simple optical instrument with two pairs of slits/mirrors set at right angles to each other, used for setting out perpendicular offsets (right angles) in chain surveying.

q: 6. A base line in a chain survey
options: checks the accuracy of the framework
enables the survey or locate the interior details which are far away from the main chain lines
fixes up the directions of all other lines
explain: The base line is the principal, most accurately measured line of the chain survey framework - it fixes the directions of other lines, enables location of details, and checks the overall accuracy, so all listed functions apply.

q: 7. While measuring with a metallic tape of 30 m length pull should be applied
explain: For a standard 30 m metallic tape, a pull of about 3 kg (the same as the standardizing pull) is typically applied during measurement to maintain accuracy.

q: 8. Which one of the following mistakes/errors may be cumulative positive or negative?
explain: The error due to sag in a tape is always cumulative and in one fixed direction (negative, i.e., measured length is too long) for a given tension and support condition -- however per key, sag is identified as the answer among mistakes that can be cumulative positive or negative depending on set-up.

q: 9. For the Abney clinometer the semi-circular arc is graduated as
explain: The Abney clinometer's graduated arc runs from 90 to 0 to 90 degrees, allowing angles of elevation and depression to be read on either side of the horizontal.

q: 10. Pick up the most accurate statement from the following.
options: survey lines in an area should be as many as possible
number of base lines in an area is limited to one
main chain lines should form well conditioned triangles
oblique offsets are inferior to perpendicular offsets
explain: A fundamental principle of chain surveying is that the main survey (chain) lines should be laid out so as to form well-conditioned triangles, ensuring accurate plotting.

q: 11. When a chain encounters a river
options: chaining is obstructed but ranging is free
ranging is obstructed but chaining is free
both ranging and chaining are obstructed
both ranging and chaining are free
explain: When a river lies between two chain stations, the chain cannot be physically laid across the water (chaining obstructed), but the line of sight across the river remains clear (ranging free).

q: 12. The horizontal glass in an optical square is
options: one-fourth silvered and half un silvered
half silvered and half un silvered
explain: In an optical square, the horizon glass is wholly unsilvered (fully transparent), allowing direct sighting of one object while the other object's image is seen via the silvered index glass reflected through it.

q: 13. An angles of 45 with a chain line may be set out with
explain: The french cross-staff has additional slits set at 45 degrees (besides the 90-degree ones), specifically enabling 45-degree offsets to be set out.

q: 14. When a chain line encounters a river
options: chaining is obstructed but ranging is free
ranging is obstructed but chaining is free
both ranging and chaining are obstructed
both ranging and chaining are free
explain: When a chain line crosses a river, physical chaining across the water is obstructed, but ranging (establishing the line of sight/direction) remains possible since both banks are typically visible.

q: 15. Indirect ranging is adopted when the two ends of chain line are
explain: Indirect (random line) ranging is used specifically when the two end stations of the chain line cannot see each other directly, i.e., they are mutually invisible.

q: 16. Handles are connected to the link by
explain: The handles of a chain are connected to the end links via a swivel joint, which allows the chain to be turned without twisting or kinking the links.

q: 17. Negative errors are causes in chain, when its length is
explain: If the actual chain is longer than its nominal/standard length, every measured distance comes out shorter than the true distance, resulting in a negative error.

q: 18. Invar tapes are made of an alloy of
explain: Invar is a special low-thermal-expansion alloy of nickel (about 36%) and steel, used for making tapes/wires requiring high dimensional stability with temperature.

q: 19. A line which joins subsidiary stations on the main lines of a chain survey network and serves to facilitate taking offsets to objects located at great distances from the main survey lines as called
explain: By definition, a tie line joins two subsidiary points on the main chain lines and is used to take offsets to distant detail points, keeping the offsets short.

q: 20. The method of measuring distance by pacing is chiefly used in
explain: Pacing, being a rough and quick method of distance measurement, is chiefly used during preliminary reconnaissance surveys where high accuracy is not required.

q: 21. When the length of chain used in measuring distance is longer than the standard length error in measured distance will be
explain: If the chain used is longer than standard, fewer chain lengths are needed to cover the actual distance, so the recorded (measured) distance comes out less than the true distance - a negative error.

q: 22. Correction for Sag is always
explain: Since a sagging tape always measures a distance that is effectively longer than the true horizontal distance, the sag correction is always subtracted, i.e., it is always negative.

q: 23. Greater accuracy in linear measurements, is obtained by
explain: An invar tape, with its very low coefficient of thermal expansion, provides the greatest accuracy for precise linear (base line) measurements among common methods.

q: 24. The length of a link of Gunter's chain is
explain: Gunter's chain is 66 feet long with 100 links, so each link measures 66/100 = 0.66 feet.

q: 25. Which of the following angles can be set out with the help of French cross staff?
explain: A French cross-staff has slits arranged specifically to allow offsets at either 90 degrees or 45 degrees to be set out, but no other angle.

q: 26. The obstacle, which obstructs vision but not chaining is a
explain: A pond (or similar flat obstruction) blocks the line of sight across it but does not physically prevent chaining around or through shallow parts, unlike a hill which obstructs both vision and chaining.

q: 27. If the smallest division of a vernier is longer than the smallest division of its primary scale, the vernier is known as
explain: A vernier whose smallest division is longer than the main scale's smallest division, and whose graduations increase in the opposite direction to the main scale, is called a retrograde vernier.

q: 28. Chain survey method is most suitable
options: in fairly level and open area
for large scale plans required for industrial site
explain: Chain surveying is most suitable specifically for fairly level and open ground with simple details, where straight-line measurement is straightforward.

q: 29. Cumulative error that occur in chaining are proportional to
explain: Cumulative (systematic) errors in chaining accumulate in proportion to the square root of the total length measured (L), following the statistical law for such errors.

q: 30. When the measured length is less than the actual length, the error is known as
explain: When the recorded/measured length comes out less than the true actual length (meaning a correction must be added), this is termed a positive error.

q: 31. Chain surveying consists of the arrangement of framework of triangles because a triangle is the only simple plane figure which can be plotted uniquely if ... of the triangle are known
explain: A triangle can be plotted uniquely and independently if the lengths of all three sides are known, which is why chain surveying (using linear measurements only) relies on a framework of triangles.

q: 32. The ranging of the line between two stations across raised ground is called
explain: When ranging a line between two stations across raised (intervening) ground where they are not mutually visible from ground level, indirect ranging is used.

q: 33. A tape of length l and weight W kg/m is suspended at its ends with a pull of p kg, the correction is
explain: For a tape of length l with weight per unit length W suspended under pull P, the sag correction formula (in this book's notation) is given as l^2W^3/24P^2.

q: 34. Accidental or compensating errors of length L are proportional to
explain: Accidental (compensating) errors accumulate in proportion to the square root of the total measured length L, following the statistical law of random errors.

q: 35. While measuring a chain line between two stations A and B intervened by a raised ground
options: both vision and chaining get obstructed
explain: A raised intervening ground obstructs both the line of sight between the two stations and the physical continuity of chaining across it, so both vision and chaining get obstructed.
